titulo: The dative: Verbs and prepositions with the dative

aula.objetivo: Form the dative in the singular and plural and use it for «for whom», age, sensations and verbs like звонить, помогать and нравиться.

sessao.titulo: Verbs and prepositions with the dative

blocos.titulo: The big distinction: LIKING vs. LOVING
blocos.explicacao: This is the most charming part of Russian, and English hides it. In English we use "love" and "like" as the same thing at two strengths: I love Maria (intense). I like coffee (milder). Both are normal active verbs with "I" as the subject. Russian splits them by structure. ЛЮБИТЬ — to love (I do the action). Люби́ть works like "love": the subject is the person, the object is in the accusative. Notice that люби́ть takes the accusative (Мари́ю, кни́гу, жену́, роди́ну). Love is an action that leaves you. You are the agent. НРАВИТЬСЯ — to be pleasing, to like (the thing comes to you). Нра́виться works differently. Russian does not say "I like coffee". It says: Мне нра́вится ко́фе. (To me the coffee is pleasing.) Мне is the dative (to me). нра́вится is the verb (is pleasing). ко́фе is the SUBJECT of the sentence. In Russian the coffee is the one acting; it pleases me. Pleasure travels from the coffee to me, and I am in the dative because it happens to me. English has the same pattern in "the coffee appeals to me" or "that idea pleases me". Two important points: STEP 1: the verb agrees with the thing, not the person. Мне нра́вится ко́фе (singular, because ко́фе is singular). Мне нра́вятся кни́ги (plural, because кни́ги is plural). The person is always мне, ему́, ей, and so on. STEP 2: do not confuse it with люби́ть. The difference in one line: люби́ть, love leaves you, you are the agent, the thing is the object, accusative. Нра́виться, pleasure comes to you, the thing is the agent, you are the receiver, dative. Which to use? If it is a deep, active feeling of yours, люби́ть. If it is something that pleases you, gives you enjoyment, comes from outside, нра́виться. In general: люби́ть is for people (romantic, family love), for one's homeland and for much-loved things. Нра́виться is for food, music, films, cities, things that give pleasure. It also works for people, when the feeling is milder than love. Russian makes you think about where the feeling comes from: love leaves you, pleasure comes to you. Two different things, two verbs, two cases.

blocos.titulo: Other uses of the dative: need, may, suit, phone
blocos.explicacao: Besides the "philosophical" uses, the dative has very practical ones. Here are the main ones. НУЖНО / НУЖНА́ / НУ́ЖНЫ — to need. In English: "I need something". In Russian: "to me [is] necessary something". The form of ну́жно agrees with the thing needed, not with the person: ну́жно when a verb follows (ну́жно рабо́тать); ну́жен when the noun is masculine; нужна́ when it is feminine; ну́жно when it is neuter; ну́жны when it is plural. The person is always in the dative: Мне ну́жно means "to me [it is] necessary". The need happens to you. НА́ДО — to need (a synonym of ну́жно). На́до works like ну́жно but is more colloquial. МО́ЖНО / НЕЛЬЗЯ́ — may / may not. Мо́жно means "it is possible, it is allowed". Нельзя́ means "it is not possible, it is not allowed". Both take the dative when the person is named. ВОЗМО́ЖНО — possible. Возмо́жно also goes with the dative. The verb НРА́ВИТЬСЯ (seen above): after "to need", it is the most common dative verb. ИДТИ́ — to suit, to look good on. Verbs of communication: помогать, звонить, писать, говорить, давать and so on. All of them put the recipient in the dative. Notice that all these verbs have a recipient, someone who receives the action, and that person goes into the dative. AGE: мне 20 лет. In English: "I am 20". In Russian: "to me [are] 20 years". The logic: age happens to you; you do not own the years. Dative.

blocos.titulo: Verbs and prepositions that take the dative
blocos.explicacao: Some verbs take the dative even when the English object looks direct: «звонить кому?» (to phone someone), «помогать кому?» (to help someone), «отвечать кому?» (to answer someone), «советовать кому?» (to advise someone). The verb «нравиться» flips the sentence: the person who likes goes into the dative and the thing liked is the subject: «Мне нравится музыка» (the music is pleasing to me). If the thing is plural, the verb is plural too: «Мне нравятся фильмы». The prepositions «к» (towards a person or place: «Я иду к другу») and «по» («по телефону», «по субботам») take the dative.

tabela.question: кому?
tabela.exemplo: Мне нравится музыка. Мне нравятся фильмы.

erros.motivo: The verb agrees with the thing that is liked.
To go to see a person, use «к» + dative.
